title: heap-buffer-overflow: vdbeRecordCompareInt THREE_BYTE_INT
live_proof: fuzz-corpus diff: the image reproduces on stock 3.22.0 under host ASan as heap-buffer-overflow in vdbeRecordCompareInt at sqlite3.c:77204
object: the serialized record vdbeRecordCompareInt decodes an integer field from. The read is aKey = &((const u8*)pKey1)[*(const u8*)pKey1 & 0x3F], an offset of up to 63 bytes taken from the record's own header byte and never checked against nKey1, followed by a read of up to eight bytes at aKey chosen by serial_type
lifetime_ender: not a lifetime defect: a corrupt record header claims a field wider than the record, and the decode reads past it
shape: read past the end of the record

status: re-measured on all four readings 2026-10-16 on this platform, and the Sublet verdict changes. host ASan was re-run on a restored x86 runtime: heap-buffer-overflow, 20 bytes after a 32-byte region, vdbeRecordCompareInt <- sqlite3BtreeMovetoUnpacked <- sqlite3VdbeExec <- sqlite3Step, identical to the 2026-10-11 bundle. virtual-malloc MISSED: open_rc=0, then s0_rc=11 and NOTRAP done, RETURNED, both controls as declared. virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT: cause=28 pc=0x3facce1760 offset 536 in vdbeRecordCompareInt at fault address 0x3facf69394, inside the arena, both controls as declared -- and it faults BEFORE s0_rc is printed, on the same statement the other arm completes. cheribsd-revocation is a NO-READING, not a miss: with the corrupt image restored the run gives s0_rc=0 s1_rc=11 and probe site 65 reports hits=0, so vdbeRecordCompareInt is never entered on that platform. The arms block is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16. THE SUBLET CELL CHANGES FROM NOT-DETECTED TO DETECTED, and this is the only case in the corpus where that arm was recorded as missing. The physical rows explain their silence as follows, quoted from results/matrix.tsv: 'The case’s own return code says why nothing was detected: s0_rc=11, SQLITE_CORRUPT -- the trigger’s database image is rejected'. That reasoning does not hold, and the two virtual arms show why on one image and one statement. Without Sublet: open_rc=0, then s0_rc=11, NOTRAP done, RETURNED -- the over-read COMPLETES, the decode returns garbage, and SQLite's own corruption check rejects the result afterwards. With Sublet: open_rc=0, then the fault, cause=28 in vdbeRecordCompareInt, before s0_rc is ever printed. So SQLITE_CORRUPT is a CONSEQUENCE of the out-of-bounds read, not a sign that the read never happened, and the defect is reached on exactly the statement whose return code was taken as evidence that it was not. That also settles the base cell: virtual-malloc is a genuine reached-and-silent, since the Sublet arm establishes reachability on the same statement and the same image. The CheriBSD cell is different and is recorded as a NO-READING: with the image restored, probe site 65 reports hits=0, so vdbeRecordCompareInt is never entered on that platform -- a different statement sequence and a different build reject the image earlier, which is the case template's own stated criterion for a real negative. The defect itself is an unchecked offset taken from the data: aKey = pKey1 + (*pKey1 & 0x3F), up to 63 bytes in, never compared against nKey1, then up to eight bytes read at aKey according to serial_type. Site 65 prints pKey1, nKey1, the header byte, serial_type, aKey and whether the widest read already passes the end. One stale cross-reference is corrected: fidelity pointed at case 34, which does not exist
fault_sites_why: Host ASan, running the same case source on stock 3.22.0, reports the invalid access in vdbeRecordCompareInt (live_proof); that run is independent of the Capstone arms and predates them.
